audit.why: Levels 1-5 to Wukong and Level 6 as the flip is a fair reading. Nimbus Strike is 10s at rank 1 against Arctic Assault's 18s, and Crushing Blow is 8s against Winter's Wrath's 9s, so his trade pattern refreshes faster than hers at every point before Glacial Prison exists. 51.6% over 188 games with one 'Skill' stage at 6 matches a lane that is genuinely close and only tips once the ultimate is up.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 'His R' spike names Cyclone as a threat to respect but gives no cooldown, and breakdown.cooldowns calls Nimbus Strike 'his only gap-close' while giving no number for it either.
audit.why: Cyclone is 130/110/90 seconds — by far the longest cooldown in the matchup — so 'back off when it is up' is only half the advice; the other half is that once he spends it the lane is yours for two minutes, which is the actual window a Sejuani wants. And Nimbus Strike is not his only gap-close: Warrior Trickster also dashes, on 22/21/20/19/18. A player counting one dash and walking into the other loses the trade he thought was free.
audit.corrected: Cyclone: 130/110/90s. Nimbus Strike: 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s. Warrior Trickster also dashes, 22/21/20/19/18s — he has two gap-closes, not one.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Cyclone 130/110/90; Nimbus Strike 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7, dash; Warrior Trickster 22/21/20/19/18, dash)

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster makes Wukong invisible while he dashes away, leaving the clone behind. Glacial Prison reveals stealth. Neither layer says so; the entry instead tells the player Glacial Prison 'travels faster than he can react with a W decoy' and to aim at 'the moving body'.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction and the entry substitutes a reaction-speed claim for it. Riot's text for Warrior Trickster is 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone' — the point of the ability is that you cannot tell which body is his, so 'aim at the moving one' is not reliable advice. Glacial Prison's stealth reveal solves it outright: the ability that hides him is answered by the ability the entry is already telling the player to throw, and nobody has told them why.
audit.corrected: Glacial Prison reveals stealth over 1300 units — Warrior Trickster's invisible dash cannot break vision on you, so the R that opens your combo is also what finds the real body.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Warrior Trickster: 'becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone')

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset and Stone Skin gives him stacking armour and health regeneration the longer he fights. Neither is mentioned; the entry treats Crushing Blow purely as an armour shred and Level 1-2 as a damage problem.
audit.why: The reset changes the tell. The dangerous moment is the attack wind-up, not the ability cast, so a Sejuani watching for a cast animation steps back a beat too late every time. And Stone Skin means every extra second in an extended trade makes him tankier — which is the exact reason the Frost-stack pattern has to be one rotation and out, something the entry asserts without ever giving the reason.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow is an auto-reset — the wind-up is the tell, not the cast. Stone Skin stacks armour and health regen the longer he fights, so one rotation and out.
sources: champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json (Crushing Blow autoReset flag; Stone Skin: 'stacking armor and max health regeneration while fighting champions')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Sejuani's resistances to 'your passive Permafrost resistances' in three places. Permafrost is her E stun and has no passive; Frost Armor comes from Fury of the North and only while she has been out of combat.
audit.why: It matters specifically against Crushing Blow, because the entry claims the shred lands 'before your passive Permafrost resistances can soften the trade'. Frost Armor is already up before the trade starts and falls off shortly after she takes damage — the true sequence is the opposite of what is written, and it is the reason a Sejuani wants to open the trade rather than absorb one.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor from Fury of the North is up before contact and drops shortly after she takes damage, so the resistances exist at the start of a trade, not the middle.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor ... persists for a short time after Sejuani takes damage')

notes: Best find: Warrior Trickster turns Wukong invisible while he dashes away and leaves a clone behind, and Glacial Prison reveals stealth. The entry already tells the player to throw R at 'the moving body' — but the whole point of the ability is that you cannot tell which body is which, so that advice is unreliable while the real answer sits in Sejuani's own ultimate and is never stated. Second: breakdown.cooldowns calls Nimbus Strike 'his only gap-close'. Warrior Trickster also dashes, on 22/21/20/19/18s, so a player counting one dash walks into the other. Third: Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset, which moves the tell from the cast to the attack wind-up, and Stone Skin stacks armour and health regen the longer he fights — the actual reason the Frost-stack trade has to be one rotation and out, a rule the entry states without ever justifying. Fourth: Cyclone is 130s at rank 1, and the entry's advice to 'back off when it is up' misses the more useful half — the two-minute window after he spends it.
